newsitem.title: JAPAN: Malay Peninsula pipeline to be built by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Malay Peninsula pipeline to be built by 2001.

text.p: A two million barrel-per-day oil pipeline will be built across the Malay Peninsula from Sai Buri on the east coast to Alor Setar on the west by 2001 at a cost of $2 billion, a Chiyoda Corp spokesman said on Monday.

A consortium comprised of Japanese, Malaysian and Singaporean firms concluded a preliminary feasibility study last November, and has decided to set up a company in April to carry out an implementation study, including drawing a basic design of the project, at a cost of $5 million, he said.
If the project proves to be economically feasible, construction will begin as early as 1999, and the pipeline is expected to be partly operational by 2001, the spokesman said.
A total of 96 oil tanks, each capable of storing 100,000 kilolitres of crude oil, will also be built at both ends of the pipeline, he added.
